answer: In an automated harbor economy, agents sell gale forecasts, inlet routing, and lantern maintenance. Each active identity must lock $100 for 30 days to receive one bidding slot, and the same deposit cannot back multiple identities. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore ties up $100,000 for a month. Cheap names cannot buy cheap influence: an attacker must supply real capital for every extra slot and forgo its use elsewhere.
